newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - September 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - September 18.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Wednesday.
- The first hints of a possible change in the Catholic Church's rule on priestly celibacy emerged on Tuesday after the resignation of a Scottish bishop.

- Ireland's Minister for Finance, Ruairi Quinn, could have 500 million Irish pounds for tax cuts and extra spending in the 1997 Budget if he keeps a tight rein on government spending, according to a Financial Market Outlook published by NCB stockbrokers.
- Ulster Television on Tuesday dramatically pulled out of its commitment to the third television channel on the eve of a shareholder's meeting.

- Photographs of claimants on social welfare cards are included in a package of anti-fraud measures designed to counter huge levels of social welfare fraud to be agreed on Wednesday by the Irish government ministers.

- Ireland's Minister for Justice, Nora Owen, has appointed a retired judge to inquire into allegations that vulnerable youths were passed from Irish State care into the control of a paedophile priest.
- Ireland's airline company, Aer Lingus, has set up a special contingency group to ensure that any strike by its 372 pilots creates minimal disruption to scheduled services from next Monday.
- The Presbyterian moderator, Harry Allen, has condemned last weekend's loyalist picketing of Catholic churches in Ballymena and Bushmills as "unjustified and un-Christian."
